propositions: Cancelled ACLI link deletes are counted as applied links due to a no-print exception handler treating any CalledProcessError as idempotent 404/409, inflating links_applied counter and hiding failures from canary.

Missing --yes flag on link create/delete subcommands causes ACLI to prompt for confirmation; with stdin=DEVNULL the prompt reads EOF, ACLI exits non-zero with 'command cancelled', and this deterministic failure repeats every pass.

The exception arm lacks output logging and idempotency markers are unchecked, so cancelled deletes produce no 'update_one: ... failed' lines and batch_outcome silently reports error=None with fabricated links_applied=N.

Idempotent marker matching must check both stderr and stdout (per acli.py:739 precedent) because link delete runs without --json, so failure output is human-readable and a 404/not-found message can land on stdout.
Adding --yes to both link subcommands (mirroring workitem delete at acli.py:714-724, bug 3256/cfd6 precedent) removes the confirmation prompt that triggers cancellation.

Extracting a new _links_failed counter and narrowed idempotent arm (matching 404/409/does-not-exist/not-found on either stream) stops the lie and makes any residual failure visible to the silent-noop canary.
